mekki-muskil:1-1.t: The saying of the Exalted {بَرَاءَة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun), nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and إلى الذين is its khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {وأذان}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to براءة, and its khabar (predicate) is إلى الناس, so it is the conjoining of a clause to a clause. It has been said that the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) is أن الله بريء من المشركين, on the assumption of "because Allah…" (لأن الله).
And His saying {من الله} in both places is a naʿt (adjective) of براءة and of أذان; for that reason beginning with an indefinite noun is good. You may also make براءة nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a declaration of disassociation". The meaning of براءة من الله is "a notification from Allah".
His saying {يَوْم الْحَج}: what governs it is the adjective of أذان; it has been said that what governs it is مخزي. It is not good for أذان to govern it, because you have already qualified it, so it has left the status of the verb.
His saying {أَن الله بَرِيء}: أنّ is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) on the assumption of the omission of the lām or the bāʾ. If you make it the khabar of أذان — but it is not the same thing as it — then the omission of the preposition must be assumed in every case.
His saying {وَرَسُوله}: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "and His Messenger is also free of the polytheists"; it was omitted because the first indicates it. Some have allowed its being nominative by conjunction with the position of the name of Allah before أنّ entered, and they said that الأذان has the meaning of "saying", so it is as if [أنّ] did not change the meaning of the speech by entering it. A group rejected that, because the open أنّ has changed the meaning of the nominal sentence (al-ibtidāʾ), since it together with what follows it is a maṣdar; so it is not like the broken إنّ, which indicates nothing but emphasis, so that its entering does not change the meaning of the nominal sentence.
As for conjoining ورسوله to the implied nominative pronoun in بريء, that is ugly according to many grammarians unless it is emphasised; but many of them allowed it in this place even without emphasising it, because the genitive phrase stands in place of the tawkīd (emphasis), so conjoining it to the pronoun in بريء is good and sound. Conjunction to an implied nominative pronoun has come in the Qurʾān without tawkīd and without anything standing in place of the tawkīd: He, exalted be His mention, said ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا, conjoining الآباء to the implied nominative pronoun. There is no proof in the entering of لا, because it entered only after the wāw of conjunction, whereas what stands in place of the tawkīd comes only before the wāw of conjunction, in the place of the tawkīd; the tawkīd, were it brought, would come only before the wāw of conjunction, as in the saying of the Exalted فاذهب أنت وربك. But that was permitted because the speech was lengthened by the entering of لا, so the length stood in place of the tawkīd.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ورسولَه in the accusative, conjoined to the wording [of the name of Allah].
His saying {من الله}: the nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; fatḥa was more fitting for it because of the frequency of use and so that two kasras would not come together. Some Arabs give it kasra according to the analogy.
«[Translator's note: the text has «في موضع التأكيد التأكيد», with the word التأكيد repeated; it is translated as two clauses.]»

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {كل مرصد}: its implied form is "at every place of ambush" (على كل مرصد); when على was omitted it became accusative. It has also been said that it is an adverb (ẓarf).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {وَإِن أحد}: أحد is nominative by its verb, its implied form being "and if anyone seeks your protection", because إن is the mother of the conditional particles, so it is more fitting that a verb follow it.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «استحارك»; the verse has استجارك.]»

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {كَيفَ وَإِن يظهروا}: the thing asked about is omitted, its implied form being "how [could it be] that you not fight them?"; it has also been said that the implied form is "how could they have a covenant?".

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {أَئِمَّة الْكفْر}: the pattern of أئمة is أفعِلة, the plural of إمام, like حمار and أحمرة. Its original form is أَأْمِمة; then the vowel of the first mīm was cast onto the quiescent hamza, and [the mīm] was assimilated into the second mīm, and the hamza with kasra was replaced by a yāʾ with kasra. This is because its due, before the assimilation, was to be replaced by an alif, since what precedes it has fatḥa, as its origin is quiescence because it is the first radical (fāʾ al-fiʿl) — it is the fāʾ of أفعلة — so its origin is substitution. Therefore it was treated by substitution after the vowel was cast onto it, and it was not treated as "between-between" (bayna bayna), as the kasra-hamza was treated in أئذا, أئنا and أئفكا; for in these the vowel of the hamza is fixed and not transferred, whereas in that one its vowel is accidental, transferred to it from the first mīm. So that one followed its origin in quiescence, which is substitution, and this other followed its origin in having a vowel, which is "between-between" in lightening, i.e. between hamza and yāʾ. I mean in all of this according to the reading of whoever lightens the second [hamza] and does not pronounce it fully.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {فَالله أَحَق أَن تخشوه}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), أن تخشوه is a badal (substitute) from it, and أحق is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. If you wish, you make فالله a mubtadaʾ and أن تخشوه a second mubtadaʾ, with أحق its khabar, and the clause the khabar of the first. It is also permissible that الله be a mubtadaʾ and أحق its khabar, with أن in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition. Similar to it is أحق أن يرضوه. أحق in both places is an afʿal [elative], with which an omission must be assumed by which the speech is completed: its implied form is "Allah is more deserving than anyone else of being feared", if you assume the preposition; and if you make أن a badal or a second mubtadaʾ, the implied form is "fear of Allah is more deserving than fear of anyone else". Likewise is the implied form of أحق أن يرضوه.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {أَن تتركوا}: أن is in the position of the accusative by حسب, and it stands in place of the two objects of حسب according to Sībawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: it is the first object, and the second object is omitted.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {أجعلتم سِقَايَة الْحَاج وَعمارَة الْمَسْجِد الْحَرَام}: in this speech there is an omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), either from its beginning or from its end. If the omission is from its beginning, its implied form is "Have you made the people of the giving of water to the pilgrims and the people of the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque like one who believes in Allah?". If you assume the omission from its end, its implied form is "Have you made the giving of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque like the faith of one who believes in Allah?". This was needed only so that the mubtadaʾ (subject) would be the same as the khabar (predicate) in meaning, and by it the speech and its sense are sound.
His saying {وَيَوْم حنين}: يوم is accusative by conjunction with the position of في مواطن كثيرة, its implied form being "and He helped you on the day of Ḥunayn".

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {لَهُم فِيهَا نعيم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of جنات. The hāʾ in فيها is for the gardens; it is a plural with alif and tāʾ by which a large number is intended. It has been said that it refers back to the mercy, and it has been said that it refers back to the good tidings, indicated by His saying يبشرهم. Likewise the hāʾ in the second فيها admits the same aspects as the first.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t:
His saying {وَقَالَت الْيَهُود عُزَيْر ابْن الله}: whoever gives nunation to عزير makes it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with ابن its khabar (predicate). On this view it is not good to drop the nunation from عزير for the meeting of two quiescent letters; the alif of ابن is not dropped from the writing, and the nunation takes kasra because of the meeting of the two quiescent letters. Whoever does not give nunation to عزير also makes it a mubtadaʾ, with ابن an adjective of it; on this view the nunation is dropped for lightness, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and because the adjective and the qualified noun are like a single noun; the alif of ابن is dropped from the writing, and the khabar is implied, its implied form being "and the Jews said: ʿUzayr son of Allah is our companion" or "our prophet". Or this implied element is the mubtadaʾ and عزير is its khabar. It is also permissible that عزير be a mubtadaʾ and ابن a khabar, with the nunation dropped for the meeting of two quiescent letters, since it resembles the letters of prolongation and softness; then the alif of ابن is kept in the writing when you make it a khabar.
Abū Ḥātim allowed عزير to be a foreign (ʿajamī) noun that is a diptote. That is far-fetched and rejected, because if it were foreign it would be fully declined, since it has three letters and the yāʾ of the diminutive is not counted, and because according to all the grammarians it is Arabic, derived from the saying of the Exalted وتعزروه.
His saying {فِي كتاب الله يَوْم}: كتاب is a maṣdar (verbal noun) governing يوم. كتاب here may not mean the Reminder, nor any other of the books, because then it would be prevented from governing يوم, since nouns that denote concrete things do not govern adverbs, as there is nothing of the meaning of the verb in them. As for في, it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, which is an adjective of اثنا عشر, which is the khabar of إنّ, as if He said: "The number of months with Allah is twelve months, established in the Book of Allah on the day He created". It is not good for في to be attached to عدة, because you would separate between the ṣila (relative clause) and the relative [i.e. the governing maṣdar and its complement] by the khabar, which is اثنا عشر.
«[Translator's note: the second paragraph concerns 9:36.]»

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying {ويأبى الله إِلَّا أَن يتم نوره}: إلا entered only because يأبى contains the meaning of preventing, and preventing belongs to the category of negation, so إلا entered for affirmation. In the speech there is an omission, its implied form being: "And Allah refuses everything they want of their disbelief except to perfect His light", so أن is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā).
And the hāʾ in the saying of the Exalted {وَلَا يُنْفِقُونَهَا} refers back to the treasures, indicated by the saying of the Exalted يكنزون. It has been said that it refers back to the wealth, because gold and silver are wealth. It has been said that it refers back to the silver, and what would refer back to the gold was omitted because the second indicates it. It has been said that it refers back to the gold, because it is treated as both feminine and masculine. It has been said that it refers back to the spending, indicated by ينفقون. And it has been said that it refers back to the gold and the silver, in the sense of "and they do not spend them [both]", but its referring back to the silver sufficed instead of its referring back to the gold, just as the Arabs say أخوك وأبوك رأيته ("your brother and your father, I saw him"), meaning رأيتهما ("I saw them both").
And the hāʾ in {عَلَيْهَا} and {بهَا}: each of them admits the aspects that were mentioned for the hāʾ in ينفقونها.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «رأبته», evidently for «رأيته». The remarks on ولا ينفقونها, عليها and بها concern 9:34–35.]»

mekki-muskil:36-36.t:
His saying {كَافَّة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the manner of your saying عافاك الله عافية ("may Allah grant you well-being"), عافيك عافية, and رأيتهم عامة وخاصة ("I saw them generally and particularly").
His saying {ثمَّ وليتم مُدبرين}: مدبرين is accusative as an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida). It may not be an unrestricted ḥāl, because His saying ثم وليتم indicates turning the back, so it is an emphasising ḥāl of what the beginning of the speech indicated, in the manner of the saying of the Exalted وهو الحق مصدقا, and His saying وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما, and like your saying هو زيد معروفا ("he is Zayd, well known").
«[Translator's note: the text reads «وعافيك عافية» as printed. ثم وليتم مدبرين is from 9:25.]»

mekki-muskil:40-40.t:
His saying {ثَانِي اثْنَيْنِ}: ثاني is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in أخرجه, which refers back to the Prophet, upon him be peace, its implied form being: "when those who disbelieved drove him out, alone among all the people except Abū Bakr"; its meaning is "one of two". It has been said that it is a ḥāl from an omitted implied pronoun, its implied form being "so he went out, the second of two". The hāʾ in عليه refers back to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, because the Prophet ﷺ already knew that nothing would harm him, since his going out was by the command of Allah, exalted be His mention, to him.
As for His saying {ثمَّ أنزل الله سكينته على رَسُوله وعَلى الْمُؤمنِينَ}, the tranquillity upon the Messenger was sent down on the day of Ḥunayn, because he feared for the Muslims and did not fear for himself; so the tranquillity came down upon him for the sake of the believers, not for the sake of fear for himself.
His saying {وَكلمَة الله هِيَ الْعليا}: all the readers have كلمة in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and that is the proper construction of the speech and more complete in meaning. Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī read it in the accusative, by جعل, and in it there is remoteness both in meaning and in iʿrāb. As for the meaning: the word of Allah has never ceased to be supreme, so making it accusative by جعل is far-fetched, because this suggests that it became so and that this occurred in it. That does not follow for the word of those who disbelieve, because it has always been made lowest in that way by their disbelief. As for its being excluded by iʿrāb: it would require that the noun not be made overt, and that it be said وكلمته هي العليا. Making the noun overt in such a case is permitted only in poetry; some have allowed it in poetry and elsewhere, and there is room for consideration in this, because of His saying وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها.
«[Translator's note: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين is from 9:26.]»

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {خفافا وثقالا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in انفروا, i.e. "go forth on foot and riding"; it has also been said that its meaning is "young and old".

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {أَن يجاهدوا}: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of في, i.e. "about striving" (في أن يجاهدوا); it has also been said that its implied form is "out of dislike of striving".

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {يبغونكم}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in ولأوضعوا خلالكم; and خلالكم is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا كتب}: ما is in the position of the nominative by يصيبنا.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {طَوْعًا أَو كرها}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "willing or unwilling".

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {أَن تقبل}: أن is in the position of the accusative by منع, and أنّ in His saying أنهم is in the position of the nominative by منع, because it is the agent.

mekki-muskil:61-61.t:
His saying {قل أذن خير لكم}: أذن is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "Say: he is an ear of good", i.e. he is a listener of good for you; i.e. he listens to what ought to be listened to and accepts what ought to be accepted. What is meant by the ear here is the whole of the owner of the ear, who is the Prophet, Allah bless him; i.e. he is a listener of good and righteousness, not a listener of evil and corruption.
His saying {وَرَحْمَة}: whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to أذن, i.e. "he is a listener of good, and he is a mercy for those who believe"; He made the Prophet himself the mercy because of how often it occurs through him and at his hands. It has been said that its implied form is "and he is one of mercy". Ḥamza read رحمة in the genitive, conjoined to خير, i.e. "and he is an ear of mercy", i.e. a listener of mercy; just as He annexed أذن to الخير, He annexed it to الرحمة, because mercy is part of good and good is part of mercy. It is not good to conjoin رحمة to المؤمنين, because the lām in للمؤمنين is redundant (zāʾida), its implied form being "and he believes the believers", i.e. he trusts them; and "he trusts the mercy" is not good — unless you make the mercy here the Qurʾān, in which case it is permissible to conjoin it to المؤمنين, and it is cut off from what precedes it. The exegesis indicates that it is connected to أذن خير لكم, because in the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd it is ورحمةٍ لكم in the genitive, and al-Aʿmash read it so; this indicates conjunction to خير, and that is the proper construction of the speech.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t:
His saying {وَالله وَرَسُوله أَحَق أَن يرضوه}: the view of Sībawayh is that the first clause is omitted because the second indicates it; its implied form according to him is "and Allah is more deserving that they please Him, and His Messenger is more deserving that they please him", so the first أن يرضوه was omitted because of the indication of the second; so on his view the hāʾ in يرضوه refers back to the Messenger, upon him be peace. Al-Mubarrad said: there is no omission in the speech, but there is a fronting and a postponing; its implied form according to him is "and Allah — that they should please Him — is more deserving, and His Messenger", so the hāʾ in يرضوه according to al-Mubarrad refers back to Allah, exalted be His praise. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "and His Messenger is more deserving that they please him", and والله is an opening of speech.
It follows from al-Mubarrad's view that "what Allah wills and you will" with wāw would be permissible, because he makes the speech a single clause, whereas that has been forbidden except with thumma. That does not follow for Sībawayh, because he makes the speech two clauses. So the view of Sībawayh is the preferred one for the verse. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), أن يرضوه is a badal (substitute), and أحق is the khabar (predicate); or, if you wish, الله is a mubtadaʾ, أن يرضوه a second mubtadaʾ, أحق its khabar, and the clause the khabar of the first. Similar to it is فالله أحق أن تخشوه, whose explanation has already passed more clearly than this.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {فَأن لَهُ نَار جَهَنَّم}: the view of Sībawayh is that أنّ is a badal (substitute) from the first, in the position of the accusative by يعلموا. Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad said: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, in the position of the accusative. The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) on these two views. Both views entail permitting the badal and the tawkīd before the completion of what is substituted for and before the completion of what is emphasised; so both views are deficient according to those versed in reasoning, because أنّ in His saying ألم يعلموا أنه is not complete before the fāʾ, so how can something be substituted for it or emphasise it before it is complete? Its completion is the condition and its apodosis, because the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of أنّ, and it is not complete except with the completion of its khabar.
Al-Akhfash said: it is in the position of the nominative, because the fāʾ has cut off what precedes it from what follows it; its implied form is "then the necessity of the Fire is his". ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: أنّ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "then what is necessary is that the fire of Hell is his". The fāʾ on these two views is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause is the khabar of أنّ. Others said: أنّ in فأن is nominative by "being established" (al-istiqrār), on the assumption of an implied genitive phrase between the fāʾ and أنّ, its implied form being "then for him is that the fire of Hell is his"; that is the view of al-Fārisī and his preference.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t: His saying {أَن تنزل}: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "of that it be sent down" (من أن تنزل). On the analogy of the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, it is permissible for it to be in the position of the genitive, intending من, because the preposition is frequently omitted with أن, so it governs while implied; and that is not permissible according to them with anything other than أن, because of how frequently it is omitted with أن specifically.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {كَالَّذِين من قبلكُمْ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a promising like what those before you were promised".
His saying {كَمَا استمتع}: the kāf is likewise in the position of the accusative, a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "an enjoyment like the enjoyment of those before you".

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His saying {وَالَّذين لَا يَجدونَ}: الذين is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to المؤمنين. It is not good to conjoin it to المطوعين, because [المطوعين] has not yet been completed as a noun, since فيسخرون is conjoined to يلمزون. So al-Naḥḥās mentioned in al-Iʿrāb, and in my view it is a mistake on his part.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t:
His saying {خلاف رَسُول الله}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it has also been said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). الخوالف are the women, and its singular is خالفة. فاعل is not pluralised as فواعل except in poetry or in a small amount of speech; they said فارس and فوارس, and هالك and هوالك. They have also said of a man خالفة and خالف when he is not noble.
And whoever reads the sīn with fatḥa in {دَائِرَة السوء}, its meaning is corruption and badness; whoever reads it with ḍamma, its meaning is defeat, affliction, harm and what is hateful. الدائرة is what encompasses a person so that he has no escape from it. It is annexed to السَّوء and السُّوء by way of emphasis and clarification, in the manner of His saying شمس النهار: even if the night were not mentioned the meaning would be known; likewise, even if السوء were not mentioned the meaning would be known from the word الدائرة alone.
«[Translator's note: the remarks on الخوالف and دائرة السوء concern 9:87 and 9:98.]»

mekki-muskil:101-101.t:
His saying {مَرَدُوا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "and of the people of Medina are people who persisted" (قوما مردوا); the genitive phrase is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and لا تعلمهم is also a naʿt of the omitted [noun].
«[Translator's note: the text writes the implied mubtadaʾ as «قوما» in the accusative, as printed.]»

mekki-muskil:103-103.t:
His saying {تطهرهُمْ وتزكيهم}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the implied pronoun in خذ, which is the Prophet ﷺ, and the tāʾ at the beginning of both verbs is for address. It is also permissible that تطهرهم be a naʿt (adjective) of صدقة and تزكيهم a ḥāl from the implied pronoun in خذ; then the tāʾ in تطهرهم is for the feminine of الصدقة, not for address, and تزكيهم is for address.
And whoever reads {مرجون} with hamza takes it from أرجأت الأمر when you postponed it; whoever reads it without hamza takes it from hope (الرجاء). This is the view of al-Mubarrad. It has been said that it too is from postponement: one says أرجأت الأمر and أرجيته meaning "I postponed it" — two dialectal forms.
His saying {قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم}: نبأ has the meaning of أعلم ("inform"), and in principle it is transitive to three objects. It may be restricted to one, but it may not be restricted to two without the third. Likewise it is not permissible to assume that من in His saying من أخباركم is redundant, because if you assumed it to be redundant, نبأ would have become transitive to two objects without the third, and that is not permissible. It has only become transitive to one object, which is نا, and then it is made transitive by a preposition. If you implied a third object, it would be good to assume من redundant according to the doctrine of al-Akhfash, because he allowed من to be redundant in the affirmative; and the implied form would be "Allah has informed us of your news, explained in detail".
«[Translator's note: مرجون and قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم are from 9:106 and 9:94. The text reads «في الجواب», evidently for «في الإيجاب» ("in the affirmative"), and is translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:107-107.t:
His saying {وَالَّذين اتَّخذُوا}: الذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is لا يزال بنيانهم.
His saying {ضِرَارًا وَكفرا وَتَفْرِيقًا} {وَإِرْصَادًا}: all of them are accusative as maṣdars (verbal nouns), and it is permissible that they be mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose).
And the hāʾ in بنيانه, in the reading of whoever reads [أسس] with ḍamma or fatḥa, refers back to whoever is the owner of the building. البنيان is the maṣdar of بنى; Abū Zayd reported بنيت بنيانا وبناء وبنية. It has also been said that البنيان is the plural of بنيانة, like تمرة and تمر.
«[Translator's note: لا يزال بنيانهم and بنيانه are from 9:110 and 9:109.]»

mekki-muskil:109-109.t:
His saying {جرف هار}: the original of هار is هائر; Abū Ḥātim said its original is هاور. Then on both views it was transposed (qalb), so the wāw or yāʾ came last, and the nunation caused it to be dropped, just as the wāw and yāʾ were dropped from غاز and رام; that is in the nominative and the genitive. Al-Kisāʾī reported تهور and تهير, and al-Akhfash reported هرت تهار, like خفت تخاف.
The grammarians allowed هار to be treated on the basis of the dropping without the dropped letter being assumed, because of the frequency of its use in transposed form, so that it becomes like a sound word: the rāʾ takes all the case endings, and the dropped letter is not restored in the accusative as is done with غاز and رام. Whoever holds this makes it on the pattern فَعَل, just as they said يوم راح and put it in the nominative, though it is transposed from رائح; but when their use of it in transposed form became frequent they made it فَعَلاً and declined it with all the case endings. It is also permissible according to them to treat it by the analogy, like غاز and رام, so its pattern is فاعل transposed to فالع, then made defective because of the heaviness of the vowel on the weak letter and the entry of nunation, just as they made defective their words قاض, رام and غاز in the nominative and the genitive, and treated them as sound in the accusative because of the lightness of the fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t: His saying {وَعدا عَلَيْهِ حَقًا}: two emphasising maṣdars (verbal nouns).

mekki-muskil:112-112.t: His saying {التائبون}: nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are the repentant", or as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar (predicate) omitted; it has also been said that the khabar is His saying الآمرون and what follows it.

mekki-muskil:117-117.t:
His saying {كَاد يزِيغ قُلُوب}: كاد contains an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-ḥadīth); therefore تزيغ follows كاد directly, and القلوب is nominative by تزيغ. It has been said that القلوب is nominative by كاد, and تزيغ is intended to be postponed, as they allowed that with كان in the like of His saying ما كان يصنع فرعون and in His saying وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا. Abū Ḥātim said: whoever reads يزيغ with yāʾ does not make القلوب nominative by كاد. It has been said that كاد contains its noun, which is the pronoun of the party, the group or the tribe, because the Companions of the Prophet, Allah bless him, were mentioned earlier; so القلوب is nominative by تزيغ, and the yāʾ and the tāʾ in تزيغ are equal, because making a plural masculine or feminine is permissible, according to the sense of "plural" and the sense of "group".
The implied pronoun was permitted in كاد, though it is not among those that enter upon a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), only because it must always be followed by a khabar, so it became like the verbs that enter upon a mubtadaʾ and khabar; hence implying its noun in it, and implying the pronoun of the matter in it, is permissible. The like of that is not permissible with عسى, because it may do without a khabar when أن occurs after it, and because its khabar can only be أن and what follows it. أن does not occur after كاد as its khabar except by poetic necessity, and likewise أن is not dropped after عسى except by poetic necessity.

mekki-muskil:121-121.t: His saying {وَاديا}: its plural is أودية. فاعل with [a plural on] أفعِلة has not come except in this one word alone.

mekki-muskil:128-128.t: His saying {عَزِيز عَلَيْهِ مَا عنتم}: ما is in the position of the nominative by عزيز, and عزيز is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول. It is permissible that ما be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and عزيز its khabar (predicate), with the clause a naʿt of رسول. And it is permissible that عزيز be a mubtadaʾ and ما an agent standing in place of the khabar, with the clause a naʿt of رسول.
